title: The Chamber Where Mirrors Become Portraits

features.name: silver-that-learns-remembering
features.desc-on-touch: The mirror-glass has aged into something between reflection and portrait. What you see is yourself, but dated—a you from three installations ago, still staring outward from behind the tarnish.

features.name: the-drying-edge
features.desc-on-touch: Emulsion pooling in the corners. Light catching on what might be varnish or might be the corruption learning to hold still-images. The portrait-mirror drinks slowly.

features.name: ownership's-threshold
features.desc-on-touch: You stand between the mirror-that-was and the portrait-becoming. The ownership is slipping. Soon neither of you will know which direction the gaze is supposed to travel.

features.name: frame-that-forgets-containment
features.desc-on-touch: Gilded wood warping at the edges. The image inside has begun to leak sideways out of its borders, and the frame no longer cares to hold it back.

features.name: the-moment-before-naming
features.desc-on-touch: Something vast hovers just behind the silver. Not quite portrait, not quite reflection. Still learning what it wants to be called.

inscription: mirrors remembered they had always been portraits of a single thing; now they know how to look away
